title: Ordinal powers: exponentiation and Cantor normal form
summary: Infinite powers describe ordered blocks and give every ordinal a unique finite normal form.
abstract: Powers of an infinite order can remain countable while describing increasingly long arrangements. Powers of the natural-number order give a way to describe every nonzero ordinal, the name for a well-order type, as a finite list of blocks. Each block is a power with a positive whole-number coefficient, and the powers decrease from left to right. This description is unique, so two ordinals can be compared by the first place where their lists differ.
